title: prices, verified against the curve's own bytecode
body: the tokens directory now shows a price in KAS, the reserve, and 24h volume — and none of it comes from any launchpad's API. kascov extracted every trade from hash-proven state changes (2,114 on mainnet: 1,600 buys and 514 sells), fetched the bonding-curve programs from chain, proved them against their own commitments, and read the curve constants out of the committed bytes — then replayed every trade against the program's own formula before publishing anything. a price only appears when the program matched a pinned build, its invariant held on every trade, and at least three real trades exercised its constants. that gate is not decoration: without it, a single transaction that buys 1,000 tokens and gifts 999 back to the curve would print a price a thousand times too high from under a dollar of spend. kascov catches that shape and refuses it. there is deliberately no market cap anywhere — a marginal price times supply overstates what could actually be taken out by 13x on the biggest token here — so kascov shows the exit value instead: what selling all circulating supply into the curve would actually return, capped by the KAS the covenant really holds. every figure that cannot be proven is an em dash, and hovering it tells you exactly why. 18 of 29 mainnet tokens price today; the ones that do not are the ones whose market programs kascov has not verified, which is the whole point. since this entry first went live the pool build joined the curve build: graduated tokens price too, each token shows its market phase (bonding with progress toward the graduation target read from the curve's own bytes, or graduated), and one covenant that had been listed as an ordinary token turned out to be the pool's LP share token — its own bytecode names it — so it is labelled lp shares and never priced. 19 of 29 mainnet tokens carry a verified price now, including the flagship.

title: tokens got their names, their art, and their whole history
body: covenant tokens carry no name and no art on chain, so kascov called KRON's tokens things like rapid-jade-narwhal and drew geometry for their logos. now the directory shows Kron Token $KRON with its picture — without trusting anyone. the names come from the launchpad's published list, and kascov checks that list against the chain before believing any of it: the genesis transaction, the covenant holding the inventory, the key that took the creator allocation, all three already proven by kascov independently, all three compared per token. 17 of 19 listings agree on everything they state; the name itself is the one part nothing can verify, so it is the only part shown as a claim, with the canonical name kept beside it. the art works the same way but harder: of the 19 logo urls published, five were already dead and three were web pages, so kascov WITNESSES instead of hotlinking — it fetches each logo once, keeps its own dated thumbnail, serves that copy forever, and re-checks the source daily. a logo that changes gets counted and dated on the token page, never silently swapped; a logo whose source dies stays alive here; and a witnessed picture wears a dashed ring so it can never be mistaken for art proven against a hash on chain. the token page also stopped showing history backwards: it used to render a token's first minutes and nothing since, and now it reads newest first with the whole life one click at a time — KRON's 1,350 events, down to the block from a minute ago. and the column that read as a price was renamed cell kas, because it never was one: it is the KAS a token's own cells must carry to exist, and the money people actually paid sits in the covenant that sold them.

title: the allocation a launch never spends is now proven too
body: a launchpad genesis funds two cells: the bonding curve's inventory, and an allocation the creator holds back. the curve trades, so a spend eventually reveals its program and kascov can check it. the creator's cell just sits there, and a cell nobody spends never reveals anything — so 9 mainnet tokens sat at unvalidated with exactly one unresolved cell, and their supply was withheld rather than guessed. they are proven now, without asking any launchpad anything. the trick is that the untouched cell's sibling from the same genesis is the same program, so it can stand in as the base; splice a candidate state into it and the chain's own commitment hash says yes or no. the missing values are in the launch transaction all along, one push per field, with small amounts riding inside the opcode itself — which is how a one-unit creator allocation stayed invisible. every candidate is still hash-gated, so a wrong guess costs a hash and never a wrong verdict. all 9 resolved inside 120 hashes each, and every genesis pair sums to a round total: 999,999,999 held by the curve plus 1 held by the creator is exactly a billion. 26 testnet tokens came back the same way. the same pass also fixed how a token gets noticed at all — one build in circulation was recognized only by a periodic catch-up sweep, so a new token using it could sit unseen until the next one ran; it is recognized the moment it is revealed now.

title: the builder guide moved inside the site
body: the 15-minute guide — compile a covenant, deploy it, spend it under its own rules, then replay that spend opcode by opcode — was the one page living outside the app, carrying its own copy of the palette and none of the site's navigation, search, or network switch. it is a page like every other one now, with a sticky rail on the left tracking which step you're reading. every link inside it goes straight to the thing it names: the playground that compiles the contract, the preflight that catches the compute-budget trap, the real coin on chain. old links keep working — /guide.html and its #trap anchor fold onto the new route — and the guide's text still ships inside the page instead of being drawn by scripts, so it stays readable to anything that crawls it.

title: a live page that stops moving under you
body: explore refreshes constantly, because the chain moves ten blocks a second — and that used to fight whoever was reading. views faded themselves out again mid-read as fresh events arrived, the mempool strip changed height as it filled and shoved everything below it, a background refresh could wipe the deploy result you were about to copy, and each cycle fired the same few requests two or three times over. now one gate shares an in-flight transfer and allows a single trailing refresh, identical confirmation fetches collapse into one, views stay visible while new data lands, the mempool strip holds one height whether it is empty or full, and the network you picked survives every navigation, reload and shared link. the pending feed also states its own health and revision, so an empty strip no longer leaves you guessing whether the chain is quiet or the feed is broken. smaller things, same theme: the explorer's section jumps became a side rail on wide screens, a token supply in the trillions compacts to fit its card with the exact number one hover away, and the focus ring kascov moves for screen readers no longer flashes a box around the heading it lands on. under the hood, kascov measures its own traffic from its own server logs — no analytics SDK, no cookie, no tracking pixel, no third-party collector — and the worker returns free heap pages to the system after building the galaxy, so its memory tracks what is live rather than the day's high-water mark.

title: the galaxy, readable at full density
body: the galaxy draws every smart coin and the moves between them, which on a network of tens of thousands of coins meant waiting a while for a picture too dense to read. it arrives in tiers now: the biggest clusters first for an immediate shape (?tier=core on /data/{network}/galaxy.json), then the outer geometry, then the identities that make each dot clickable. a dot never claims an identity it hasn't actually received — placeholder dots aren't clickable, and a tier whose layout no longer matches the identities it was handed drops them rather than mislabel a coin. focusing a small cluster at the edge keeps its surroundings in view instead of stranding you in empty space, the camera never zooms backwards, a click lands on the dot you can see rather than a generous invisible circle around it, and touch gets a target it can actually hit while still letting the page scroll.

title: watch covenants before they land: the pending lane
body: kascov followed only confirmed history. now it watches the mempool too. a per-network poller reads the node's pending transactions a few times a second, classifies the covenant ones with the exact rules the confirmed follower uses, and surfaces them in a live pending lane in explore. a genesis, transition, or burn shows up the instant the node sees it, then clears the moment a block confirms it, or fades if the mempool drops it. on a ten-block-per-second chain a covenant tx lingers only a heartbeat, so this is the closest kascov gets to real time. read from your own node's mempool, no third-party feed. GET /data/{network}/pending serves the current set, and the live stream carries pending and pending_resolved events.

title: kascov now runs on its own Kaspa node
body: the whole stack moved onto hardware I run and watch: a mainnet node, a testnet node, the indexer, and the site, all on one machine, off the cloud. it matters for what kascov is. every covenant you see is decoded from a node I run myself, not a public resolver that prunes deep history and abandons the cursor under load. it also unlocked the pending lane, because a live mempool feed needs a node you control. verify from chain, now from my own chain view.

title: trade buttons, from where a token launched
body: tokens launched on a supported launchpad now show a trade button on their kascov page. kascov works out where a token launched from an on-chain fact, the art host committed in the token's own genesis payload, not a handshake or a maintained list. KaspaRocket is the first supported launchpad, and adding the next one is a few lines. the verified art got tidier too: once proven against the sha256 committed at launch, the real image now fully replaces the generated icon instead of peeking out behind it.

title: a window that read 3 events, brought back to nearly 70,000
body: an outage weeks ago left a slice of testnet-10 history that every reachable node had pruned. a community node operator had been running an archival node through exactly that window and shared it. kascov walked their archive from inside the gap and merged what it found: close to 70,000 covenant events, back in the timeline, verified as canonical chain history rather than asserted. it is a big partial recovery, not a complete one, because even that archive had pruned some block bodies, and the recovery tool says so honestly. history you can check, not history you take on faith.

title: the art is real: hash-verified token images
body: a launchpad adopted the on-chain naming recipe within a day — real tokens now launch with their name, ticker, and image hash committed in the genesis payload. so kascov now renders the art itself: the worker fetches the deployer's image, proves the bytes against the sha256 committed on chain, and serves them from kascov's own origin at /img/{network}/{id}. match: the art appears over the coin's avatar. mismatch: it doesn't, and the page says why. nobody can swap a token's face after launch, and kascov never hotlinks a byte it hasn't proven. verified, not asserted — now in pictures.

title: real token names, read from the chain itself
body: a launchpad shipped with a verify-on-kascov button and asked the obvious question: why no real names? because kascov only shows what the chain proves — and until now, nobody's token name lived on chain. now there's a way: put {"name": …, "ticker": …} in the genesis transaction's payload at launch, and kascov reads it, shows it first, and badges it 'named on chain' — honestly labeled as a deployer claim, with the canonical name always alongside. the recipe is in the guide. names from private databases still don't appear here, and never will: verified, not asserted.

title: open doors: badges, a front door for the API, and honest timestamps
body: builders can now embed a live 'verified on kascov' badge in any README — /badge/{network}/{id}.svg re-renders from chain state on every fetch, so it stays honest by construction. the API grew a machine-readable front door at /data/{network}/index.json (production logs showed integrators guessing URLs on first contact — now a guess lands somewhere useful), every event now carries its accepting block's real header timestamp and blue score (stored since the capture migration, served never — until now), and share pages stopped shooing crawlers away, so the site can finally be indexed. under the hood: the shutdown backup now runs smallest-database-first so mainnet's snapshot always fits the grace window, and archives went hourly.

title: speaking the standard: KCC-1 template identities
body: covenant conventions are becoming a real standard — KCC-1, drafted by Romain Billot with Michael Sutton and Ori Newman — and kascov now speaks it. every conformance vector from the draft passes as a unit test in the new kcc1 module, KCC20 reveals carry their canonical template hash (3 identities across 2,889 verified reveals, each recomputed independently to check our own math), coin pages and the templates panel display them, /data/{network}/template/{hash} looks them up, and new spends record the draft's leader/delegator input ordering. tracking the draft honestly, not claiming compliance: it is a draft, and the vocabulary may still move.

title: the gap, healed — and an honest hole
body: testnet-10's frozen window is back: 60,789 events, 47,956 spends, and 48,469 state cells re-derived straight from the chain and promoted into the live index — 13,297 covenants got their history back. honesty where it's owed: the oldest slice of the gap had already been pruned from every reachable node before recovery could touch it, and that part is gone for good. the chart shows the hole rather than papering over it. this loss is exactly why the next entry exists.

title: kascov runs its own kaspa node now
body: production's testnet-10 follower now reads from kascov's own archival node over a private link instead of public resolver nodes — block fetches went from internet round-trips to sub-millisecond hops, catch-ups that took a day now take minutes, and archival mode means nothing the node has seen ever gets pruned again. mainnet joins it on dedicated hardware next.

title: the follower learned to fail loudly
body: testnet-10 froze for 49 hours and the dashboard said nothing — never again. the sync follower now probes whether its cursor is actually walkable (a block can exist and still be a dead end after a deep reorg), forces recovery when it's moving without progressing, and reports 'stalled' on /health instead of pretending. email alerts fire within minutes, backups stream every 5 minutes with verification (the old uploader silently choked on databases past 1GB), and a gap-recovery tool can rebuild lost windows from the chain itself while it's still within node retention.

title: will this transaction pass? find out before you broadcast
body: the playground grew a third mode: paste a transaction as JSON and preflight it — every input's compute budget checked against the classic 'script units exceeded' trap, masses measured against the block limit, an honest fee estimate, and a real script-engine run for inputs that carry their witness. every finding comes with its fix, plain as 'set computeBudget: 10'. your transaction goes into the call and nowhere else — nothing broadcast, nothing kept.

title: built with covenants — and a feed to follow it
body: the landing page now showcases what builders are shipping on Kaspa's smart coins, starting with the Kaspa Covenant Game Kit by @w00c00 — 1v1 games on player-funded covenant escrow, its contract verified byte-identical on kascov. and everything on this page is now an Atom feed at /feed.xml, so your reader hears the news before your timeline does.

title: every transaction gets a page
body: paste any txid — in search, or from any timeline — and land on its own page: which smart coins it touched, what was born, moved or retired, the cells it created and spent, the decoded token actions, and a one-click replay of the real spend through Kaspa's actual script engine. older workers still answer with the coin links; nothing breaks.

title: friends check each other's math
body: a new consistency endpoint cross-checks kascov's token accounting against other independent ecosystem indexers, automatically — token counts, supplies, the lot. differences usually mean one of us has a bug; we fix ours and share theirs kindly.

title: verified from the chain — not asserted
body: the accounting layer: every KCC20 token's history replayed, supply conservation checked, every live balance cryptographically proven against its commitment. 258 of 270 tokens verified, 0 invalid, the rest honestly marked with reasons. token pages show holders, classified mint/transfer/burn timelines, and the proof.

title: the galaxy glows and the front page breathes
body: coins are glowing orbs now, clusters are nebulae, the map sits on a parallax starfield — and the landing page's blockDAG is a living simulation: blocks born at kaspa's cadence, linking to parents, drifting like time. all of it pauses the instant you look away, so it costs nothing.

title: the mainnet galaxy tells the truth
body: small networks now show their actual coins — glowing dots with their shared-transaction links — instead of two giant summary bubbles hiding four covenants. click a dot, get the coin.

title: the chain has names now
body: the decoder learned genesis0, PURE and KCC20 from the chain's own revealed programs — thousands of covenant runs went from anonymous hex to real contract names, decoded and re-checkable by anyone.

title: the first open KCC20 token directory
body: every covenant token on the network in one table — owner and amount decoded straight from chain state, honestly badged "decoded, not validated" until the accounting layer proves them. plus USD context on mainnet and event filters everywhere.

title: an API worth building on
body: a cursorable event feed for the whole network, batch coin lookups, webhook secrets with signed deliveries, a live KAS price endpoint — and a builders guide at /guide: deploy, spend, replay in 15 minutes.

title: find, follow, replay
body: search all coins by name, id or contract from any page; coin pages update live as events land; and any real spend replays through Kaspa's actual script engine, opcode by opcode.

title: every coin link is a billboard
body: share a coin anywhere and it unfurls into a live picture card — name, avatar, holdings, story. plus a sitemap, so search engines can finally find the coins.

title: the big-network wave
body: the galaxy streams in tiers (big clusters first, the rest behind), the grid paginates instead of downloading everything, and quiet tabs stop refetching — kascov now scales past 168k coins without breaking a sweat.

title: analytics · the network at a glance
body: births against retirements over the whole history, coins by contract type, a survival curve, and the indexer's own reorg ledger — every chart drawn from the same feeds the page already serves.

title: make a smart coin without writing code
body: pick a covenant, fill in the parties and amounts in plain terms, and deploy it on testnet-10 in one click — byte-perfect script assembled in your browser, no toolchain.

title: a page for every coin
body: coin pages no longer depend on the loaded grid window — deep links, galaxy clicks and shared URLs resolve straight from the indexer, for all 168k+ coins.

title: the galaxy
body: the whole network on one zoomable map — every app at once, each dot a smart coin, each link a shared transaction. scroll to zoom, click a dot to open its life story.

title: kascov.io
body: the explorer gets its own front door — old links forward, share cards re-rendered, canonical everywhere.

title: first outside hands
body: community pull requests land — bug fixes from strangers and the covenant workbench unified into one playground. open source doing its thing.

title: the workbench wave
body: what-if spend simulation, cryptographically verified contract source, a visual script debugger, a ZK proof-verification panel, and payload lanes — the tools a covenant developer actually needs, in the browser.

title: contracts RUN now
body: deploy a real covenant, spend it, watch the program reveal itself on-chain permanently — plus escrow settlement, multi-contract app families, and a mission-control redesign with the BlockDAG as the hero.

title: stories get honest
body: multi-piece coins tell their true story, truncated histories get archival repair, "retired" is reserved for the story-ending burn — and a contract generator so you can make one yours.

title: the scale rework
body: the monolithic snapshot era ends: paginated grid, address pages, a live SSE event stream, template analytics and a daily digest. kascov stops being a demo.

title: coins learn to speak
body: friendly names, life stories, spend-time decoding that captures the program a covenant actually ran, and SilverScript recognition by skeleton — byte-identical, not guesswork.

title: day one
body: an acceptance-driven covenant indexer, a post-Toccata script disassembler, a lifecycle lab CLI, a live Cloud Run worker and a dashboard — kascov goes from empty repo to watching testnet-10 breathe, in one day.
